name: Common Travel Area (CTA) — British Citizens

requirements.blocker_text: This requires British citizenship. No visa, no permit, no residence application is required — reciprocal rights predate EU membership and were reaffirmed by the May 2019 Memorandum of Understanding, unaffected by Brexit.

sources.title: Brexit - Common Travel Area (CTA) - Government of Ireland

notes: GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE BILATERAL ARRANGEMENT, the only route of its kind across this entire multi-country dataset — no visa, no permit, no residence application whatsoever for British citizens moving to Ireland, and the reverse also holds for Irish citizens in the UK (see uk's own file structure, not separately encoded here since this file represents the Ireland-side view). Rights confirmed: live, work (including self-employment), study, access healthcare, social welfare, social housing, and — genuinely unusual — VOTE in local and national parliamentary elections without naturalising, a real and substantial political right most other countries in this dataset reserve strictly for citizens. Pre-dates EU membership entirely and was explicitly reaffirmed as unaffected by Brexit via the May 2019 Memorandum of Understanding — a genuine confirmation that this arrangement survived the broader UK-EU relationship's dissolution. CRITICAL SCOPE LIMIT: CTA rights do NOT extend to non-Irish/British family members of a British citizen exercising CTA rights — they must use Ireland's normal immigration rules (see ie_family_reunification), family_can_join marked false here specifically to reflect that the CTA mechanism itself carries no family-extension right, even though the British citizen's own path is completely unrestricted.
